findings.evidence: CSS sets h1 to Georgia, serif and h1 em to italic, but Georgia has no CJK glyphs: the headline renders in the fallback CJK sans (Noto Sans CJK SC) and '履历' is a synthetic slant. The 'serif display with italic accent' is a Latin-font recipe applied to Chinese text.
findings.before: font: 400 76px Georgia, serif; h1 em { font-style: italic }
findings.after: Name a CJK display face (e.g. Noto Serif SC / Source Han Serif) and mark emphasis with weight or colour, not a faked oblique.
findings.why: The recipe was copied rather than chosen: what renders is neither the intended face nor a real italic.
findings.title: The intended font actually renders
findings.fix: Fix the font load (path, format, font-display) and wait for fonts before capture.
